## Data Flow: Task Execution

```
1. USER CREATES TASK
   ↓
   POST /api/sdlc/tasks
   ↓
   SDLCTaskManager.create_task()
   ├─ Generate unique task_id
   ├─ Set status = "created"
   ├─ Save to JSON
   └─ Return task object
   ↓
2. START PIPELINE
   ↓
   execute_stage(task_id, "analysis")
   ├─ Load task from storage
   ├─ Set status = "analyzing"
   ├─ Save task
   └─ Start agent async
   ↓
3. RUN ANALYSIS AGENT
   ↓
   OllamaAgentRunner.run_analysis(task, project)
   ├─ Build system prompt
   ├─ Build user prompt (task description + context)
   ├─ Call Ollama LLM via HTTP
   ├─ Parse JSON response
   ├─ Create AgentResult
   └─ Log to structured JSON
   ↓
4. SAVE RESULTS
   ↓
   task.agent_results["analysis"] = AgentResult
   task.save_task()
   ├─ Serialize to JSON
   ├─ Write to data/tasks/{task_id}/task.json
   └─ Update task.updated_at
   ↓
5. ADVANCE PIPELINE
   ↓
   _advance_or_complete(task)
   ├─ Check next stage
   ├─ If more stages: execute_stage("backend")
   └─ If done: status = "pending_approval"
   ↓
6. REPEAT FOR EACH STAGE
   ↓
   analysis → backend → n8n → frontend → qa → pending_approval
   ↓
7. HUMAN APPROVAL
   ↓
   POST /api/sdlc/tasks/{id}/approve
   ├─ Verify status = "pending_approval"
   ├─ Update status = "done"
   ├─ Save task
   └─ Return success
   ↓
8. TASK COMPLETE ✓
```

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                   Frontend Dashboard                         │
│  ┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐  │
│  │ • Projects Tab → List/Create projects                 │  │
│  │ • Tasks Tab → Create/View tasks                       │  │
│  │ • Pipeline Tab → Kanban board with drag-drop          │  │
│  │ • Each task card shows: ID, title, status, agent      │  │
│  │ • Click task → Modal with full details                │  │
│  │ • Approval button shows only if pending_approval      │  │
│  └───────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘  │

│  └───────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘  │

           ↕ HTTP

│  • Returns: JSON response                                   │
│  • Used by: All 5 agents                                    │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

## Key Design Patterns

### 1. State Machine (Task Status)
```
created
  ↓
analyzing → analysis_approved
  ↓
backend_running → (human_review or error)
  ↓
n8n_running
  ↓
frontend_running
  ↓
testing
  ↓
pending_approval
  ↓ (human clicks approve)
done
```

### 2. Agent Pipeline
```
Each agent:
- Takes: Task + Previous results
- Runs: Ollama LLM with context
- Outputs: JSON (structured)
- Stores: In task.agent_results
- Next: Pass results to next agent
```

### 3. Async Execution
```
HTTP request
  ↓ (sync)
Queue task
  ↓
Return 200 OK to client
  ↓ (async background)
Execute pipeline
  ↓
Update task state
  ↓
Client polls GET /api/sdlc/tasks/{id}
```

### 4. Structured Logging
```
Each operation:
1. Log entry created (JSON)
2. Includes: timestamp, level, logger, message, custom fields
3. Rotating file (10MB max)
4. Queryable via API
5. Human-readable + machine-readable formats
```

## Deployment Architecture

### Development (Local)
```
Your Machine
├─ Backend (Python) :8003
├─ Frontend (Node) :5173
├─ Ollama :11434
└─ Data files (./data, ./logs)
```

### Production (Docker)
```
Container Host
├─ Backend Container
│  ├─ Python 3.12 + FastAPI
│  ├─ Port 8003 (exposed)
│  └─ Volumes: ./data, ./logs
├─ Frontend Container
│  ├─ Node build + Nginx
│  ├─ Port 80 (exposed)
│  └─ Proxies /api to backend
└─ Ollama Container
   ├─ LLM service
   ├─ Port 11434 (exposed)
   └─ Volumes: ollama_data
```

### Cloud (Render)
```
Render Deployment
├─ Web Service (Backend)
│  ├─ Python runtime
│  ├─ Auto-deploy from GitHub
│  └─ https://taskloom-backend.onrender.com
├─ Static Site (Frontend)
│  ├─ Node build
│  ├─ Nginx CDN
│  └─ https://taskloom-frontend.onrender.com
└─ External Ollama
   ├─ Render or other provider
   └─ OLLAMA_HOST env var
```

## Scalability Considerations

### Current (File-based)
✓ Single instance
✓ File I/O bottleneck ~1000 tasks
✗ No concurrency control
✗ No backup/recovery

### Phase 2 (Database)
✓ PostgreSQL for ACID
✓ Connection pooling
✓ Concurrent requests
✗ Agent execution still single-threaded

### Phase 3 (Distributed)
✓ Multiple backend instances
✓ Load balancer
✓ Message queue (Celery/RQ)
✓ Redis caching
✓ Ollama cluster

## Security Architecture

```
Client
  ↓ HTTPS/TLS
API Gateway
  ↓ CORS validation
Backend
  ├─ Input validation (Pydantic)
  ├─ Rate limiting (future)
  └─ Error handling (no info leaks)
  ↓
Data Storage
  ├─ File permissions
  ├─ No secrets in code
  └─ Environment variables only
```

## Monitoring & Observability

```
Application Logs
  ↓
┌─────────────────────┐
│ JSON Log Format     │ → Can be shipped to ELK/Splunk
│ - timestamp         │
│ - level             │
│ - logger            │
│ - message           │
│ - task_id (custom)  │
└─────────────────────┘
  ↓
Log Query API
  ├─ GET /api/logs → search/filter
  ├─ GET /api/logs/stats → aggregates
  └─ GET /api/health → uptime
```

---

## Summary

Task Loop uses a **layered architecture** with clear separation of concerns:

1. **User Layer**: Dashboard, API, CLI
2. **API Layer**: FastAPI routes with middleware
3. **Business Logic**: Task/Project managers + orchestration
4. **Agent Layer**: Ollama-powered AI agents
5. **Persistence**: JSON files (local) / PostgreSQL (production)
6. **External**: Ollama LLM service

This design enables:
- ✅ Easy to understand
- ✅ Simple to modify
- ✅ Straightforward to scale
- ✅ Observable and maintainable
- ✅ Production-ready
"}}

│  │  11434       │          │  ./data/     │                      │
│  │              │          │  ./logs/     │                      │
│  └──────────────┘          └──────────────┘                      │
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

## data flow: task execution

```
1. user creates task
   ↓
   post /api/sdlc/tasks
   ↓
   sdlctaskmanager.create_task()
   ├─ generate unique task_id
   ├─ set status = "created"
   ├─ save to json
   └─ return task object
   ↓
2. start pipeline
   ↓
   execute_stage(task_id, "analysis")
   ├─ load task from storage
   ├─ set status = "analyzing"
   ├─ save task
   └─ start agent async
   ↓
3. run analysis agent
   ↓
   ollamaagentrunner.run_analysis(task, project)
   ├─ build system prompt
   ├─ build user prompt (task description + context)
   ├─ call ollama llm via http
   ├─ parse json response
   ├─ create agentresult
   └─ log to structured json
   ↓
4. save results
   ↓
   task.agent_results["analysis"] = agentresult
   task.save_task()
   ├─ serialize to json
   ├─ write to data/tasks/{task_id}/task.json
   └─ update task.updated_at
   ↓
5. advance pipeline
   ↓
   _advance_or_complete(task)
   ├─ check next stage
   ├─ if more stages: execute_stage("backend")
   └─ if done: status = "pending_approval"
   ↓
6. repeat for each stage
   ↓
   analysis → backend → n8n → frontend → qa → pending_approval
   ↓
7. human approval
   ↓
   post /api/sdlc/tasks/{id}/approve
   ├─ verify status = "pending_approval"
   ├─ update status = "done"
   ├─ save task
   └─ return success
   ↓
8. task complete ✓
```

## component interaction

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                   frontend dashboard                         │
│  ┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐  │
│  │ • projects tab → list/create projects                 │  │
│  │ • tasks tab → create/view tasks                       │  │
│  │ • pipeline tab → kanban board with drag-drop          │  │
│  │ • each task card shows: id, title, status, agent      │  │
│  │ • click task → modal with full details                │  │
│  │ • approval button shows only if pending_approval      │  │
│  └───────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘  │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
           ↕ http (json)
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                 backend api server                           │
│  ┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐  │
│  │ routes (fastapi):                                     │  │
│  │  • get /api/sdlc/projects                             │  │
│  │  • post /api/sdlc/tasks                               │  │
│  │  • post /api/sdlc/tasks/{id}/approve                  │  │
│  │  • get /api/logs                                      │  │
│  │  • get /api/health                                    │  │
│  └───────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘  │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
           ↕ http
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│              ollama llm server                               │
│  model: qwen3.5:0.8b                                        │
│  • takes: system prompt + user prompt                       │
│  • returns: json response                                   │
│  • used by: all 5 agents                                    │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

## key design patterns

### 1. state machine (task status)
```
created
  ↓
analyzing → analysis_approved
  ↓
backend_running → (human_review or error)
  ↓
n8n_running
  ↓
frontend_running
  ↓
testing
  ↓
pending_approval
  ↓ (human clicks approve)
done
```

### 2. agent pipeline
```
each agent:
- takes: task + previous results
- runs: ollama llm with context
- outputs: json (structured)
- stores: in task.agent_results
- next: pass results to next agent
```

### 3. async execution
```
http request
  ↓ (sync)
queue task
  ↓
return 200 ok to client
  ↓ (async background)
execute pipeline
  ↓
update task state
  ↓
client polls get /api/sdlc/tasks/{id}
```

### 4. structured logging
```
each operation:
1. log entry created (json)
2. includes: timestamp, level, logger, message, custom fields
3. rotating file (10mb max)
4. queryable via api
5. human-readable + machine-readable formats
```

## deployment architecture

### development (local)
```
your machine
├─ backend (python) :8003
├─ frontend (node) :5173
├─ ollama :11434
└─ data files (./data, ./logs)
```

### production (docker)
```
container host
├─ backend container
│  ├─ python 3.12 + fastapi
│  ├─ port 8003 (exposed)
│  └─ volumes: ./data, ./logs
├─ frontend container
│  ├─ node build + nginx
│  ├─ port 80 (exposed)
│  └─ proxies /api to backend
└─ ollama container
   ├─ llm service
   ├─ port 11434 (exposed)
   └─ volumes: ollama_data
```

### cloud (render)
```
render deployment
├─ web service (backend)
│  ├─ python runtime
│  ├─ auto-deploy from github
│  └─ https://taskloom-backend.onrender.com
├─ static site (frontend)
│  ├─ node build
│  ├─ nginx cdn
│  └─ https://taskloom-frontend.onrender.com
└─ external ollama
   ├─ render or other provider
   └─ ollama_host env var
```

## scalability considerations

### current (file-based)
✓ single instance
✓ file i/o bottleneck ~1000 tasks
✗ no concurrency control
✗ no backup/recovery

### phase 2 (database)
✓ postgresql for acid
✓ connection pooling
✓ concurrent requests
✗ agent execution still single-threaded

### phase 3 (distributed)
✓ multiple backend instances
✓ load balancer
✓ message queue (celery/rq)
✓ redis caching
✓ ollama cluster

## security architecture

```
client
  ↓ https/tls
api gateway
  ↓ cors validation
backend
  ├─ input validation (pydantic)
  ├─ rate limiting (future)
  └─ error handling (no info leaks)
  ↓
data storage
  ├─ file permissions
  ├─ no secrets in code
  └─ environment variables only
```

## monitoring & observability

```
application logs
  ↓
┌─────────────────────┐
│ json log format     │ → can be shipped to elk/splunk
│ - timestamp         │
│ - level             │
│ - logger            │
│ - message           │
│ - task_id (custom)  │
└─────────────────────┘
  ↓
log query api
  ├─ get /api/logs → search/filter
  ├─ get /api/logs/stats → aggregates
  └─ get /api/health → uptime
```

---

## summary

task loop uses a **layered architecture** with clear separation of concerns:

1. **user layer**: dashboard, api, cli
2. **api layer**: fastapi routes with middleware
3. **business logic**: task/project managers + orchestration
4. **agent layer**: ollama-powered ai agents
5. **persistence**: json files (local) / postgresql (production)
6. **external**: ollama llm service

this design enables:
- ✅ easy to understand
- ✅ simple to modify
- ✅ straightforward to scale
- ✅ observable and maintainable
- ✅ production-ready
"}}
